comparisons.objective: Extract and recover a spacer with a pusher; candidate replaces a motion-control harness connector.
comparisons.physical_skill: Indirect tool pushing and part recovery versus connector unlatching, extraction, alignment, mating, and cable/seal management.
comparisons.success_condition: PR has measured exit, nest, tool-return, release, and containment gates; candidate lacks equipment geometry, procedure, and any defensible completion or damage rubric.
comparisons.reason: The tested ability is constrained indirect extraction with a separate tool, not electrical connector replacement.

comparisons.objective: Loosen a captive nut with a selected wrench and swing a latch arm open; candidate replaces a harness connector.
comparisons.physical_skill: Wrench fitting, torque-limited turning, and arm articulation versus connector latch manipulation and controlled mating.
comparisons.success_condition: PR measures nut backoff, arm angle, clearance, dwell, rounding, and force limits; candidate has no connector-specific thresholds or inspection criteria.
comparisons.reason: Fastener release and arm opening test a different contact sequence from connector extraction and installation.

comparisons.objective: Stretch and seat an O-ring in a hydraulic-plug groove; candidate replaces a harness connector while preserving seals.
comparisons.physical_skill: Deformable-ring expansion, placement, and twist control versus rigid connector unlatching and mating with unspecified seal management.
comparisons.success_condition: PR defines maximum stretch, seating, tilt, twist, and release; candidate does not identify the seal type, handling requirement, or measurable acceptance state.
comparisons.reason: Seal preservation is only a constraint in the candidate; the PR directly tests deformable O-ring installation.

comparisons.objective: Start and tighten a bracket bolt with a ratchet in confined access; candidate replaces a confined harness connector.
comparisons.physical_skill: Thread starting and short-stroke ratcheting versus latch release, extraction, keyed alignment, mating, and cable handling.
comparisons.success_condition: PR proposes thread capture, seating, torque, tool return, and release, though its live scorer is unqualified; candidate lacks any executable connector rubric.
comparisons.reason: Confined access is shared, but the central tested mechanics—threaded fastening versus connector mating—are meaningfully different.

comparisons.objective: Hand-install a spin-on oil filter within a prescribed post-contact turn range; candidate replaces a harness connector.
comparisons.physical_skill: Thread engagement and controlled hand rotation versus connector latch manipulation and translational mating.
comparisons.success_condition: PR tracks thread retention, gasket contact, hand-driven rotation, and over-tightening; candidate lacks part, pose, latch, seal, and damage thresholds.
comparisons.reason: The PR tests threaded gasket compression, not electrical connector replacement.

comparisons.objective: Install a circlip in a shaft groove and verify it by turning; candidate replaces a harness connector.
comparisons.physical_skill: Pliers-driven elastic spreading, planar control, groove seating, and verification versus connector extraction and mating.
comparisons.success_condition: PR defines over-spread, twist, cocking, seating, tool release, and verification; candidate has no measurable connector acceptance rubric.
comparisons.reason: Retaining-ring installation is a different force-control and geometry problem.

comparisons.objective: Join an open drive chain and slide a forked keeper under two pin heads; candidate replaces a harness connector.
comparisons.physical_skill: Aligning chain ends over pins and transverse keeper insertion versus connector latch release, axial extraction/mating, and cable/seal management.
comparisons.success_condition: PR measures pin/hole alignment, slot retention, cradle pose, release, stability, and containment; candidate lacks corresponding connector geometry and thresholds.
comparisons.reason: Both include retention, but the PR tests multi-part chain-joint assembly rather than a plug-and-receptacle replacement.

comparisons.objective: Immerse, time, withdraw, and replace a wafer using pliers; candidate replaces a harness connector.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tool grasp, bath immersion, timed bimanual button operation, and precise wafer replacement versus connector service manipulation.
comparisons.success_condition: PR specifies immersion duration, timer timing, clearances, heater-pin placement, drops, and contamination hazards; candidate has no executable rubric.
comparisons.reason: The manipulation sequence and hazards are unrelated to connector replacement.

comparisons.objective: Seat an add-on circuit board over two rows of header pins without bending them; candidate replaces a motion-control harness connector.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both require fine multi-contact alignment and controlled electrical mating; the PR uses parallel board-to-header insertion, while the candidate additionally claims unlatching, extraction, cable, and seal handling.
comparisons.success_condition: PR measures board height, two-axis tilt, pin-bend history, release, and stability; candidate does not identify connector geometry, pins, latch, insertion depth, or damage/seal tests.
comparisons.reason: The core tested ability may reduce to alignment and controlled electrical mating, and the candidate lacks enough geometry or rubric to establish a meaningful distinction.

comparisons.objective: Drive opposed tapered shims behind a door jamb until snug without bowing it; candidate replaces a harness connector.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual opposed wedge insertion and structural-gap force control versus connector unlatching and mating.
comparisons.success_condition: PR defines orientation, overlap, snugness, jamb bow, release, and rest; candidate lacks any measurable service outcome or damage limits.
comparisons.reason: Wedge loading and jamb deformation control are different from connector replacement.

comparisons.objective: Latch two buckle tongues and a chest clip around a doll; candidate replaces a harness connector.
comparisons.physical_skill: Harness positioning and multiple buckle/clip closures versus confined electrical connector extraction, keyed mating, and cable/seal preservation.
comparisons.success_condition: PR measures tongue insertion, clip closure/location, seat motion, head clearance, release, and stillness; candidate lacks connector-specific success and safety gates.
comparisons.reason: Although both involve latches, the PR tests restraint placement and multiple buckle closures, not component replacement.

comparisons.objective: Rotate and clamp an angle-grinder guard toward an operator position; candidate replaces a harness connector.
comparisons.physical_skill: Lever release, guarded rotation, and reclamping versus connector latch manipulation and controlled mating.
comparisons.success_condition: PR defines guard angles, lever state, grinder pose, hand clearance, and misuse faults; candidate has no comparable numeric rubric.
comparisons.reason: Rotational guard adjustment is mechanically different from extracting and installing a connector.

comparisons.objective: Remove a coin cell, discard it, and latch a replacement in a socket; candidate replaces a harness connector.
comparisons.physical_skill: Small-cell extraction, polarity-aware placement, and socket-latch closure versus plug extraction/alignment/mating with cable and seal management.
comparisons.success_condition: PR measures disposal, cell pose, polarity, latch closure, release, stability, drops, and board damage; candidate lacks part identity, latch geometry, mating depth, seal inspection, and damage criteria.
comparisons.reason: Both are replacement tasks with latching, but the PR specifically tests planar coin-cell handling and polarity, not cable-connector mating.

comparisons.objective: Load four connector modules into a hinged frame and squeeze the frame shut until it clicks; candidate replaces one motion-control harness connector.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both involve connector-component alignment, insertion, retention, and latching; the PR adds repeated module placement and frame closure, while the candidate claims extraction plus cable/seal management.
comparisons.success_condition: PR defines module seating, frame click, empty positions, trapped-module failure, clearance, and dwell; candidate provides no part, access, insertion, latch, seal, or damage rubric.
comparisons.reason: The tasks may share the same essential insertion-and-latching ability, and the underspecified candidate does not establish that its claimed extraction or seal work is actually tested.

comparisons.objective: Recover drawer motion by compressing clothing that obstructs it; candidate replaces a harness connector.

comparisons.objective: Set date bands, ink a stamp, stamp a marked box, and return the tool; candidate replaces a harness connector.

comparisons.objective: Unhook a hot air-fryer basket and place it on a mat using only its handle; candidate replaces a harness connector.
